title: COMBINE FIRE
full_story:
The Xenia Fire Protection District reports that emergency crews were dispatched yesterday just after 3:15 pm to the intersection of County Road 2200 North and 540 East in rural Wayne County.

Upon arrival, firefighters found a combine completely engulfed in flames.  Seven crew members battled the blaze using a pumper, a brush truck, and a tanker.  While firefighters were able to get the flames under control and cleared the scene in just over an hour, the machine was declared a total loss.

No injuries have been reported, and the cause of the fire remains under investigation.

title: NORTH CLAY SCHOOL BOARD
full_story:
The North Clay School Board met in Louisville Wednesday night to handle a busy agenda.

During public comment, local resident Marie McGee urged the board to allow homeschooled students to participate in the district’s extra-curricular activities and athletic programs.

In personnel action following a closed session, the board voted unanimously to dismiss paraprofessional Lindsey Fehrenbacher effective immediately.  To fill staffing needs, board members approved posting for a new full-time paraprofessional and an anticipated part-time bus aide, while also granting administration the authority to hire non-certified positions as needed.  Additionally, an unpaid leave request for Cindy Rose was approved.

The board also took action on a student disciplinary case, voting seven-to-zero to expel a student for the remainder of this school year and the entirety of the next academic year.  However, the expulsion has been stayed, and the student will instead be placed on school probation.

On a positive note, administrators highlighted that the Pre-K program has earned another Gold Star level designation.  Superintendent Keith Price also recognized Bus Safety Week, giving a special thanks to the transportation department for hosting an elementary safety assembly featuring a robotic vehicle named “Buster the Bus.”

title: KINMUNDY MAN DIES
full_story:
An investigation is underway in Marion County after an eighty-year-old Kinmundy man fell to his death Wednesday afternoon north of Salem.

Marion County Coroner Claude Howell says the body of William Hawkey was discovered around eight o’clock Wednesday night at a maintenance building on Hotze Road.

Investigators believe Hawkey climbed a ladder to the roof to remove tree limbs sometime between one and three in the afternoon.  While on the roof, Hawkey reportedly stepped onto a skylight and fell twenty feet to the packed rock floor below.

He was not found until hours later, when a relative went to the property after Hawkey failed to return home.  Coroner Howell pronounced Hawkey dead at the scene from blunt force trauma to the head.

Authorities say Hawkey maintained the building and nearby oil wells for an out-of-state owner.

The Marion County Sheriff’s Department and United Medical Response both assisted at the scene.

title: HAUNTED THEATER
full_story:
Nostalgia Theater presents Demented Holidays tonight and tomorrow night from 7 to 11 pm each night.  This will be a walk-through haunted house.  Nostalgia Theater is located in downtown Flora in the former Town Theater building.

This year’s haunted house experience is even better than last year.  The thrills start with a pitch-dark haunted maze, a tour through terror-filled holidays, and a trip through the basement horrors.  Two stories of haunts await those that dare.

Ticket price is $10 per person and all tickets will be sold at the door.  This event may not be suitable for young children.

Money raised will be used for the continuing restoration of Nostalgia Theater.

Other upcoming events at Nostalgia Theater include the children’s Christmas play on December 4th and 5th, the Christmas Madrigal dinner and performance on December 13th, and as always Nostalgia Theater is available to rent for your upcoming events and holiday parties.  For more information, call 618-676-4496.

title: NORTH WAYNE SCHOOL BOARD
full_story:
The North Wayne School Board covered a wide range of district business at its latest meeting, signing off on personnel moves and sparking a community conversation on future facility upgrades.

Topping the evening’s agenda, board members green-lit several routine items under the consent agenda.  This included the approval of the September 23rd budget hearing and regular meeting minutes, personal leave and dock day requests, and FMLA leave for two district employees.  The board also cleared school facility use for Pee Wee Basketball practices and authorized the payment of the September bills.

In policy developments, the board adopted the Press Plus Policy Issue 122 updates and approved the North Wayne Community Unit School District 200 Risk Management Program.

District infrastructure was also a major talking point.  Board members held an open discussion regarding a potential district building project.  While no official action was taken, the session gave local residents the opportunity to ask questions and share feedback on the prospective project.

Following an executive session, the board returned to open session to officially hire Betty Diefenbach as a full-time bus driver.

title: STORM SPOTTER TRAINING
full_story:
The Effingham County Emergency Management Agency in collaboration with the National Weather Service in Lincoln will be holding a Special Storm Spotter Training Class tomorrow, from 10 am to Noon at the Effingham County Emergency Operations Center, 311 Miracle Avenue, Effingham.

During the regular storm spotter training, participants will learn the characteristics of severe thunderstorms and other associated threats, severe weather-relevant cloud formations, and weather safety practices.

Participants will also learn how they can be a National Weather Service SKYWARN volunteer and help keep their community safe, by providing timely and accurate reports of severe weather directly to the National Weather Service.

In addition to the usual storm spotter training, the NWS is providing a winter storm outlook with safety information, and the NWS will also explain ways they provide incident support to first responders.

The class is free and open to the public and pre-registration is NOT required.

For questions about the training, please call Effingham County Emergency Management Agency, 217-540-1669.

title: SOUTHERN ILLINOIS RAIL GRANT
full_story:
US Representative Mike Bost announced that he has helped secure $25.1 million in federal funding for Evansville Western Railway to improve approximately 124.5 miles of freight rail infrastructure stretching from Evansville, Indiana to Okawville, Illinois.

“Southern Illinois has always played an important role in keeping America’s economy moving, and our railroads are a big part of that,” said Bost.  “Whether it’s moving coal, agricultural products, or other critical materials, our businesses depend on safe and reliable transportation to get the job done.  I’m proud to see this investment coming to our region because it means stronger infrastructure, safer rail operations, and more opportunities for the hardworking folks who call Southern Illinois home.  I’ll keep working to make sure our communities have the resources they need to grow and succeed.”

The funding, awarded through the Federal Railroad Administration’s Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements Grant Program, will support major upgrades to the railway’s tracks, equipment, and maintenance facilities.  The improvements will strengthen rail safety, improve service reliability, and support the efficient transportation of American-made energy products throughout the region.

The project will include replacing rail and ties, installing hot bearing detectors to identify potential equipment failures, constructing a new locomotive maintenance facility, and rehabilitating 12 locomotives.  These improvements will help modernize the short-line railroad, reduce the risk of equipment failures, and ensure more dependable freight service for businesses throughout Southern Illinois and Southwestern Indiana.

title: BLAKE FEHRENBACHER SCHOLARSHIP
full_story:
Frontier Community College announced that applications are now available for the Blake Fehrenbacher, RN Memorial Scholarship.  The $1,000 scholarship is designed to support students currently enrolled in an accredited health science program.

Eligible fields of study include nursing, pre-medicine, physical therapy, pharmacy, radiography, medical office professions, medical transcription, and other health-related disciplines as determined by the scholarship committee.  Applicants must demonstrate financial need and the ability to successfully complete their program of study.

Recipients will be selected based on several criteria, including demonstrated effort, determination, and dedication to their chosen health science field.  Applicants must also be students in good academic standing, exhibit financial need, demonstrate compassion toward others, and have a strong record of merit and scholarship.

The application deadline is January 8th.  Scholarship applications can be downloaded from the scholarship page on the Frontier Community College website.

For more information about available scholarships, visit the Frontier Community College scholarship webpage at https://iecc.edu/fcc/admissions-aid/scholarships.

title: IDOA TO HELP WITH OPEN ENROLLMENT
full_story:
The Medicare open enrollment period is now underway and older adults looking to change their existing Medicare plan can receive free, personalized assistance through the Illinois Department on Aging’s (IDoA) Senior Health Insurance Program (SHIP).

“It is that time of year where people with Medicare will encounter numerous advertisements about the various Medicare Health and Drugs plans for 2027.  Don’t go it alone, let us put your mind at ease when you discuss your options with a certified SHIP counselor and make an educated choice,” said Illinois SHIP Director Sandy Leith.

During open enrollment, which runs through December 7th, people who are already enrolled in Medicare have the opportunity to review their current coverage and switch to a different plan for the following year.

To make this process easier for Medicare beneficiaries and their caregivers, Illinois’ SHIP program offers statewide health insurance counseling services through a network of 300 sites and 1,000 trained and certified counselors.  Illinois has trained 200 new SHIP counselors over the past year, and all counselors have received additional training on how to assist you during Open Enrollment.

SHIP counselors can answer questions about Medicare, Medicare Advantage plans such as HMOs and PPOs, Medicare Part D drug plans, Medicare Supplement policies, Retiree Group Insurance, and other health insurances.  All services are free, and SHIP counselors do not sell or solicit any type of insurance.

Aside from open enrollment assistance, SHIP counselors can also help soon-to-be eligible individuals with Medicare sign-up questions.  To find a SHIP counselor near you, call the statewide Senior HelpLine at 1-800-252-8966 or email [email protected].
